Comments: On August 6, 2024, the Department of Oil and Gas inspector, Cody Murray, conducted an onsite inspection of the HERBERT C SMITH 193D (Permit # 021-20852), operated by VESSELS COAL GAS INC.. • There is no visible well posting and no well tag ID on the well anywhere to be found. The hand written ID no longer legible. • The well appears to be not in use as it is disassembled in a few places. • The well valves are open to the pipeline and the surface is rusted entirely. • The well head appears intact with no signs of leaking. • OGI used an RKI GX-3R Pro to detect for the presence of gas and no gas was detected. • The 2023 annual production and mechanical assessment reports have not been submitted. • The most recent production report of 2019 indicated the well "Active" - Well Temporarily not producing. • The department requests the operator provide proof of production of the well and when it was last in use. Based on today’s inspections the following violations will be issued: Posting OGA3211(G) - Failure to install permit number and operator information. OGA3211(H) - Failure to install permit number on well. MIA 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect well quarterly for Mechanical Integrity Assessment. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit annual report to the Department for Mechanical Integrity Assessments. APR 78.121(A) - Failure to submit annual production report. 78.121(B) - Failure to electronically submit Annual Production Report to the Department.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/18/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 982864
Permit API: 117-22132
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/18/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's OMR 02-188 well site located in Hamilton Township, Tioga County on 1/18/2023 at 1020 hours. The weather was 39 degrees with cloudy skies. An Act 9 sign, site plans and onsite inspection log are all located at the site entrance. The inspection was conducted to summarize remedial activities from a reported release on 11/29/2022.Excavation work of the areas where a reported release of produced water on 11/29/2022 impacted has now been completed. The excavated fill slopes have been covered with plastic (photos #4 and 5). Post excavation attainment soil samples and waste characterization samples were collected by the operator on 12/8/2022. Repsol provided a Notice of Violation (NOV) response to the DEP on 12/13/2022. The NOV response has been uploaded to eFACTS.The majority of the site remains permanently stabilized with vegetated cover. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. Recently hydraulically fractured wells continue to flowback at this time. Containment structures remain intact. Post-construction stormwater management controls remain in place. Pooled water on the pad surface that was field measured for electrical conductivity today ranged from 640 to 905us/cm. There was no evidence of any new spills/releases.Violations cited against API #117-22132 on 11/30/2022 remain outstanding at this time. No additional violations are noted. I departed the site at 1140 hours.

Comments: This was a follow up inspection concerning gas that had been detected on the outside of the surface casing. During this inspection, gas was not detected anywhere outside of the surface casing. That being said, the 1/4" tube running from the tubing to the surface casing was pinched open. Since there is no check valve on this line to prevent gas from the tubing to enter into the surface casing, we request one be tied in. We also request that we receive a report on what has been done since the NOV was received. This may have eliminated the problem. Once this is done, we will continue to monitor the well, but the violation would be closed.

Violation ID: 8173915

Comments: On 1/29/2024, DEP representative John Rogers attended a Pre-Construction Meeting for installing a new power line for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. The weather was 29 degrees and overcast. Approximately four inches of snow covered the location. Seneca's Kirk Gregory and Kurt Klepper met me at the start of the power line project along North Road. We reviewed the Electrical Line section of the Taft ESCGP. The electrical line will be supported by power poles for the first 900 feet and then will be installed underground for the remaining 1500 feet. The powerline and poles will be installed by Wellsboro Electric. The underground portion will be excavated and buried by JL Watts Excavation. The plan calls for timber mats and a temporary bridge to cross wetlands and a creek. Kirk expects Wellsboro to start setting poles on 2/5/2024 with the excavation crew starting sometime after that. Kirk discussed flagging of the wetland areas prior to construction. After the meeting, I inspected the well location. I met the company man, Carlos Martinez prior to inspecting the well site. Carlos explained current operations as follows: The Patterson 805 drilling rig was being set up on site in preparation for drilling surface and intermediate on five new wells. The rig is expected to start drilling the 109HU at 1800 today. Carlos expects it to take six days to drill the two sections on each well. Another rig is scheduled to be brought in to drill the kickoffs and laterals for each well.Carlos accompanied me on the site inspection. The rig and ancillary equipment were stationed on secondary containment. Chemicals were staged in secondary containment. Crews were preparing the drill cuttings collection area. Half round roll off dumpsters were being stationed over secondary containment in this area. Drill cuttings will be solidified with wood pellets prior to being transported to a waste disposal site. During the inspection I did witness a channel of water along the northeast corner of the pad that field tested at as high as 4.2 mS conductance. I did collect sample #9551-081 for laboratory analysis of the water near where the outfall from the pad surface flows down to the MRC basin. I could see a current the water flowing towards the outfall but did not witness water draining over and down the outfall during the inspection. Snow covered this section of the pad.Due to snow cover, site stabilization could not be adequately assessed during the inspection. PCSM is addressed by three retention berms and an MRC BMP with constructed wetland. I did witness water and ice being retained in retention berm 3 and the MRC basin.After the inspection I did discuss the area of elevated conductance with Carlos. We did discuss possible causes being ice melt or cement used during pad construction.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the unprotected pad surface is a violation of CSL 402(b). Additional violations may be cited based on the sample results.Because of the large volume of elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to the unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid impacting the unprotected pad surface.The DEP recommends the following:1. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid at the northeast side of the pad; clean/report as necessary.2. Continue to monitor the stability and functionality of the retention berms and the MRC basin.I left the site at 1300 hours.

Comments: On 1/27/19 at 0945 hrs., I conducted an inspection in response to a crude oil release that was reported to the Department on 1/25/20, and initially was discovered on 1/24/20. The release occurred near Howard Drilling, Inc.'s TLC 1 well (API 063-32818) in Conemaugh Twp., Indiana Co. According to initial reports, and verified by Mr. Dale "Wally" Howard via telephone on 1/27/20, approximately 80 barrels of crude oil was transferred from stock tanks at two nearby wells (063-22666 and 063-31878) during plugging operations, to two 100 barrel holding tanks located adjacent to Hogue Drive. According to Mr. Howard, the holding tanks belong to Tunnelton Liquids Company (property owner). ARG Refining was scheduled to pick the oil up on 1/24/20. There are several erosion rills formed with the resulting sedimentation, E&S controls need to be installed immediately. Violations for erosion and sedimentation will be issued if controls are not installed. The report for the clean-up and restoration of the area needs to be submitted to the Department and approved before violations can be lifted.

Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/20/2025
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of about 20 gallons of produced fluid. The release occurred while a water truck was removing fluid from the temporary storage tanks onsite.Tobias arrived onsite to screen and remediate the impacted area. A vac truck was used to remove some fluid and surface material. The rest of the remediation involved scraping an area that was approximately 100' long by 63' wide. The excavation averaged 1-2" deep with occasional depths of about 8". There was about 40 tons of material removed and placed into 2 dumpsters for disposal.There were some puddles on the pad surface that were screened for conductivity. Those readings ranged between 0.49 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) and 1.07 mS/cm. Soil conductivity immediately off the pad and behind the release ranged between 0.15 - 0.18 mS/cm while a puddle in that area was 0.45 mS/cm (Photos 4 and 5). Continuing downslope, conductivities of puddles in the compost filter sock (CFS) were 0.87 - 1.01 mS/cm. The readings continued to drop as the downslope infiltration berms were screened. The conductivity in front of the berm was 0.37 mS/cm and behind the berm it was 0.1 mS/cm. Moving east along the pad and uphill from the release soil conductivities ranged between 0.70 and 0.83 mS/cm and conductivities of puddles were between 1.03 and 1.09 mS/cm.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted and Immediately Corrected for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). It is recommended that the pad be screened under the secondary containment when it is eventually removed.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/03/2025 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8227911
Permit API: 123-47902
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/03/2025
Comments: The R H Stevenson Lease 4 conventional well is the nearest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the R H Stevenson lease. The tank battery is situated within earthen containment and consists of an upper level containing two stock tanks, and a lower level containing two polyurethane tanks. The stock tanks are plumbed into PVC piping that extends along the rear of the upper level of the earthen containment until terminating into the first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level. The first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level is also equipped with additional PVC piping apparently for the purpose of either removing or depositing fluids into the tank in the lower level of containment. At the time of this inspection, standing pools of fluid present in the upper level of the containment were found to have specific conductance measuring 5,980 microSiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). It was observed that straw had been laid down beneath the PVC piping in the upper level of containment. Where the straw cover ends, fluid was found to be actively flowing from the upper level of containment to the lower level. No fluid was observed to be flowing through the PVC piping connecting the stock tanks to the polyurethane tank during the time of this inspection. Neither polyurethane stock tank was found to have a noticeable volume of fluids contained within them at the time of this inspection. Some accumulation of fluids and crude oil could be observed around the base of the polyurethane tanks in the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection. The flow of fluids from the upper level to the lower level of containment was not found to be accumulating nor increasing the accumulated volume of fluids and crude oil present at the bottom of the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection.Approximately 40 feet south of the lower level tank battery containment area, crude oil and production fluids emerged on the soil surface. This flow of fluids continues west and is visually impacted by crude oil for approximately 180 feet. From there, soils and standing fluid with elevated specific conductance continue for approximately 75 feet before reaching a culvert. A pool of fluid at the entrance of the culvert was found to have specific conductance measuring 6,820 uS/cm.From the culvert, the fluid continues southwest in the natural swale for approximately 115 feet before reaching a point at which the swale transitions to an unnamed tributary (UNT) stream of Jackson Run, with defined bed and banks. At this point, waters in the UNT had specific conductance measuring 5,510 uS/cm. Specific conductance of 2,750 uS/cm was observed in the waters of the UNT in the remaining approximately 180 foot stretch, at which point there is a confluence with a second UNT of Jackson Run. Immediately before the confluence, waters in the impacted stream with specific conductance of 1,923 uS/cm were observed. Approximately two feet downstream of the confluence at a point with coordinates 41.95555, -79.29740 was the apparent end of impact to the UNTs of Jackson Run, where waters in the stream had a measured specific conductance of 42.6 uS/cm.At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the well.On 04/04/25 I called and spoke with William Cenk and Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. Mr. Cenk and Mr. Miller agreed to meet with Department officials onsite next week. A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Comments: Onsite for a routine inspection. The well appears to be producing and is properly labeled. A vertical separator is located inside a stone dike that is lined. It appears that the lined-stoned dike is leaking collected stormwater through the dike. Water has channeled and traveled to the rock ditch located on the outside of the pad. This area should be monitored for potential releases/pollution from the separator and piping. A 210bbl steel tank is inside a lined containment.According to Scott Lux (DEP WQSS) the NOV's identified on 1/27/2020 for inspection #: 2988353 relating to the frac tank and release to the ground have been corrected. A new containment area has been installed with a 210bbl steel tank. Observations indicate that a release has occurred inside of the containment. Oil absorbent pads are floating inside the containment during the inspection. There are also several large areas, just outside on the north side of the secondary containment that were observed to indicate a release had occurred to the ground. The site has not been restored according to state regulations for restoration. The documents onsite all appear to be the original plans and documents. The Emergency Response Plan and PPC Plan should be reviewed and updated to reflect proper ownership/operator information.NOV's noted

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Chevron Appalachia Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-12-06
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 870897
Permit API: 129-28979
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: South Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-12-06
Comments: The inspection is being conducted in response to a spill reported by Chevron on 12/5/2019. Aqueous and soil samples are being collected in addition to the inspection. More of the secondary containment has been removed since the previous inspection. The pad smells strongly of petroleum. Chevron representative Gene Barchetti is present on site. Additional breaches in secondary containment are now visible. Multiple areas around and between the well heads, and to the south of the the well heads, have significant quantities of drilling mud and/or staining (Photos #1, 2, 3, 6, 7, and 8). Larger quantities of stormwater have been contaminated than previously observed. Stormwater discharging from under secondary containment still in place south of the well heads has a rainbow sheen (Photo #4); the large puddle below this discharge also has a sheen (Photo #3). Gene Barchetti was shown the discharge and the sheen. Stormwater has transported and concentrated drilling mud to the NE corner of the pad (Photo #5) and into a stormwater channel downslope. Both the NE pad corner and downslope in the stormwater channel have the strongest petroleum smell encountered on the site. Multiple pieces of equipment not in use remain without secondary containment. A significant portion of secondary containment remains. The Department requests photographic documentation of conditions under the remaining containment obtained during removal activities. Based on the 5 barrel release estimate in the Initial Report of Incident as documented in Inspection Record #2971125 and evidence gathered and reported in this inspection and Inspection Record #2970703, the Department recommends remediating the spill pursuant to 78a66(c)(2).

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: OIL & GAS MGMT INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/10/2026
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8267122
Permit API: 111-20223
Unconventional: No
County: Somerset
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/10/2026
Comments: On March 10, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management's Neilan 1 well located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4106039.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the wellhead. Attached to this wellhead was a small metal production tank, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of this production tank either.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed some production equipment and a meter box on site. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this meter box or the production equipment attached to it.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site that both appeared to be connected to the well. The tank on the left did not have any observable holes or corrosive parts, however, the tank on the right still had several corroded pipes at the base of the tank and a pipe that was completely broken in half due to corrosion at the top of the tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near either production tank at this time.The Department obtained soil conductivity readings at the base of the production tank near the corroded piping. Readings of 0.74ms, 0.42mS, 0.56mS, were obtained. These readings appeared elevated in comparison to the background soil conductivity reading obtained of 0.09mS. It does not appear any remediation has occurred on site at the time of this inspection.Soil conductivity readings under the pipe were collected in the same localized location during the Department's previous inspection documented in IR 4106039 where it was 1.285mS. Therefore, since neither evidence of remedial actions were observed, nor a response from the operator has been received, the violations for a release remain outstanding as it appears the release may be diluting and/or migrating into the surrounding soil/subsurface areas.During IR 4106039, the Department requested the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of that inspection report. The written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, a plan for remediation of the spill or release, and how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requested the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon its receipt. To date, the Department has yet to receive the aforementioned documents.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from broken and corroded piping off of a production tank on site is remaining outstanding at this time.

Violation ID: 8173634
Permit API: 129-28930
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Salem Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/29/2024
Comments: On January 29, 2024, inspection conducted at the Fatur Well Pad in Salem Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow-up to IR 3700597, which was conducted by DEP WQS at OGI request. During this inspection, a pink oily substance with elevated conductivity was discovered on the ground next to the onsite GPU unit and within its secondary containment. Violations were issued as a result. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The access road and well pad appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 2 and 3). The compressor noted in IR 3700597 had rags remaining within its secondary containment, soaking up what appears to be a petroleum based substance (see photos 4 and 6). However, it is on the verge of overflowing (see photo 7). No elevated conductivity readings were gathered from this substance (see photo 8), and there did not appear to be any staining on the ground around it. The well head onsite (well 10H) was equipped with a well tag and appeared to be in production (see photos 13 and 14). Pooling was observed on the ground around the well head, however this appeared to be snowmelt due to the low conductivity and lack of discoloration (see photo 15). A Hugill's dumpster was observed on the eastern side of the pad dripping a dark fluid onto the ground (see photo 16). Although this fluid was not elevated in conductivity, the DEP recommends that this is addressed by the operator and necessary remediations are conducted if this is a regulated substance. The pink oily fluid observed during the time of IR 3700597 remains in the GPU secondary containment. The conductivity of this substance read 15,990 Microsiemens at the time of inspection (see photo 18). The disconnected hose and pink tinted substance remains on the gravel behind the GPU unit. The conductivity of this substance and/or ground surface read 724 Microsiemens at the time of inspection (see photo 19). The gear lubricant container holding a substance of similar coloration remains adjacent to the GPU unit (see photo 20). What appears to be a pump attached to the GPU unit was observed to be completely frosted over at the time of inspection (see photo 21). What appears to be an additional pump in disuse was observed on the ground adjacent to the GPU unit. A background soil conductivity reading was taken at the edge of the woods adjacent to the eastern side of the pad, which read 155.5 Microsiemens. Of the five additional tanks and equipment placed in secondary containment onsite that were not previously noted (see photos 3, 9, 11, 12, and 22), three of them appeared to be holding rainwater at the time of inspection. This does not comply with 25 PA Code 78a64a, as they appear to be reduced in capacity by at least 10 percent at the time of inspection, increasing the likelihood of discharge to the ground in the event of a spill. The ERP and PPC plan were found in the mailbox attached to the Act 9 sign (see photos 24 and 25).The DEP recommended in IR 3700597 that the operator ensure the structural integrity of the all production equipment is sound and properly contain and dispose of any production related fluid in accordance with current regulations to prevent any future pollution events. The DEP also recommended in IR 3700597 that the operator assess the red tinted fluid observed on the ground near the GPU as well as inside of the containment and remediate any spills in accordance with current regulations.Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that not all necessary corrective actions has been taken for site to comply with current regulations. Violations remain outstanding, additional violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of operator response.

Comments: On 10/6/20 at 0955 hrs., I conducted an inspection of PA General Energy Co., LLC's J Elmer Lockhart 1127 well (API 063-32044) in Grant Twp., Indiana Co. in response to a reported release of brine/production fluid from a vent at the well head. The well was shut-in by the operator on 10/1/20, prior to the release. A well tag is affixed to the well head. A site ID sign with the operator's name, address, phone number, and well permit should be posted pursuant to OGA 3211(G). On 10/5/20, the operator reported a release of brine/production fluid from a vent between casing strings to the Department. The exact amount of fluid released is unknown, but it was initially estimated as a couple of barrels. Upon inspection of the release area, the size of the impacted area appears to be consistent with a multi-barrel release. The fluid impacted an area at the well head, then flowed down an access road to a lower area where the landowner has various junk vehicles staged. At the time of inspection, Huey Brothers had excavated the lower area and access road. Moody & Associates has been contracted as a consultant and was field screening for soil conductivity. PID screening was yielding no readings. On 10/7/20 I received an update from Nathan Harris with PGE stating that the excavation of the lower area was reaching depths of 10-12 feet in spots, due to the released material hitting an area of weathered rock and migrating vertically.The release of production fluid/brine from the well head constitutes violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1), and CSL 402(b). The violations associated with this release will be resolved upon remediation of the site and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Please refer to page 3 of this Notice of Violation regarding a written response describing how you intend to remediate the release and demonstrate attainment of an Act 2 standard.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/22/2023
Comments: On 3/22/23 an incident inspection of the Mac Well Pad site was conducted in response to a report of a spill that was reported to the Department on 3/21/23. Background:On 3/21/23 I received a call from DJ Hardy of EQT. He informed me that he had reported a spill to the Department's telephone hotline. The spill had occurred on the Mac Well pad when flowback was being conducted. EQT was investigating the cause of the spill but it appeared that the flowback had resulted in sand settling in the first tank in the series. The sand had caused the level of fluid in the first tank to fill faster than the subsequent tanks. The level rose and was released out of a valve at the top of the tank. The produced fluid misted out of the valve into the secondary containment, onto the gravel pad, and onto the northwestern vegetated slope of the well pad. SPSI had been contracted for remediation. Mr. Hardy stated he estimated that approximately 20 gallons of brine were released. I scheduled a field meeting with Mr. Hardy for the next day (3/22/23).During the inspection the following was observed:-An Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo #1).-Some residual sand was observed on the side of the tank that had overflowed, and some impacted fluid was observed in the secondary containment (Photos #1-4).-The secondary containment appeared to be structurally sound, and no evidence of leaks were detected (Photos #5-8).-Substrate appeared to have been excavated from the spill area and fresh gravel was observed (Photos #8-10).-Vegetation had been removed from the northwestern pad slope (Photos #11-12). According to Mr. Hardy, the production fluid misted the vegetation but did not appear to saturated the soil below the vegetation.-Two roll-off containers were present on the pad (Photo #13). Mr. Hardy stated that only one container was needed for the waste.-No elevated conductivity was observed in the spill area, immediately outside of the spill area, on the pad berm, or on the vegetated pad slope (Photos #15-18).According to Mr. Hardy, the spill outside of the containment has been remediated. EQT plans to clean the tanks, flush, and vacuum out the secondary containment to dispose of any impacted fluid.Violations of 78a57(a), SWMA 301, and 78a54 are being noted as immediately corrected.

Comments: On 02/01/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone conducted an administrative report for Chesapeake Appalachia LLC's (CALLC) STONE BRA location. This location is currently in flowback operations after fracking the STONE N 3HC and STONE N 104HC wells. This report is in response to a spill notification (CTS # 354624) received on 01/30/2021 at 0900 hours. The purpose of this report is to document details regarding the reported release, remediation actions taken thus far by CALLC, and to cite violations. On 01/30/2021, Tony Savitski (CALLC) reported that at 0900 hours, a mixture of rainwater and produced water spilled to the pad surface due to a hole in a containment structure. An estimated 42 gallons was reported as released. An estimated 20' x 20' area of impacted soils has been excavated and stored on containment, pending sample results for proper disposal. It was reported that no fluid escaped from the pad. On 02/01/2021, I contacted Eric Hottenstein (CALLC) at 0845 hours in order to gather more details regarding the release. Mr. Hottenstein stated that a frac tank storing produced fluids and stationed within secondary containment leaked fluid into containment. A hole in containment, believed to be caused by a hose puncture, resulted in the mixture of rainwater and produced fluid to leak to the pad surface. Mr. Hottenstein estimated that approximately 10 tons of impacted soils had been excavated and stored in containment. Mr. Hottenstein stated CALLC plans to pursue ACT 2 remediation. Samples for ACT 2 purposes have been collected and the frac tank containment has reportedly been fixed. Photos of the site have been forwarded by Mr. Hottenstein and attached to this report. The release of 42 gallons of the rainwater and produced fluid is in violation of Pa. Code 78a.56(a), CSL 402(b), and SWMA 301. Due to the quantity of the reported release, it is requested that CALLC refer to and remediate in accordance with Pa. Code 78a.66. This release is referred to the DEP's Bureau of Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8284378
Permit API: 123-46784
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/12/2026
Comments: Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) reported a release of produced fluids at TMP's Brown Hill Road tank battery. The tank battery consists of five 210 bbl stock tanks (# 1053, 1054, 1055, 1056, 1057), a separator, gas meter, burner, and buried brine tank. The Brown Hill Church Lease, Lyszaz Lease, and R Brown Lease are plumbed to this tank battery.It was reported that lightning from recent thunderstorms must have struck the tanks, ignited combustible contents, and caused an explosion that expanded and ruptured four out of the five tanks. The released fluid flowed through the ruptures and into the secondary containment area. It was reported that at the time of the release, the stock tanks were mostly empty but did contain some sludge from prior storage of produced fluids.Brian Bennett of TMP was onsite at the time of this inspection to discuss cleanup expectations with Evan Bruce (WQS) and I (Mathew Haemer - WQS). Brian estimated that the volume of the released fluids was approximately 4 bbl. Brian explained that he had been working on mixing sawdust with the sludge that had filled the containment area and had begun to remove the saturated sawdust to temporary storage in barrels staged inside the secondary containment area.At the time of this inspection, the buried brine tank was nearly empty. The majority of the release pooled around the buried brine tank. Brine was not reported to be a suspected component of this release. However, elevated SPC readings were observed both in the sawdust/sludge mixture (5,350 uS/cm) and in the soils of the secondary containment area's western end (8,900 uS/cm).Two groundhog holes were observed in the northwest corner of the secondary containment area. Elevated SPC readings (4,140/12,250 uS/cm) were observed in the soil inside of the groundhog holes. This indicates that at one point in time, brine discharged into the secondary containment area rose to a level sufficient to spill over into the holes, and from that point migrate outside of containment. A storage yard has been constructed downslope of the tank battery. HDPE pipe is scattered at one end, and spare pump jacks at the other. Coincidentally, the soil is visibly wet beneath the area where the HDPE pipe is scattered. Elevated SPC of soils (1,468 uS/cm) was observed where the pipe is scattered. The disturbed earth above the pipe and pump jacks also had elevated SPC readings (1,346 uS/cm). A violation for failure to construct and maintain a method of secondary containment which satisfies requirements under 40 CFR 112 is being cited due to the evidence that brine was able to migrate through the secondary containment wall via the groundhog holes and/or through permeating the earthen containment.The quantity of the release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold set forth in the Department's spill policy, therefore either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required. It is requested that the source and extent of the release be identified.
